title: App Service: plans, slots and swap with warm-up

videos.script: Lesson 7 updated the shop in place, and nobody answered while it restarted. Lesson 8 fixed that with revisions. This lesson fixes it a third way. {{plan}} App Service starts with a plan. The plan is the machines: a size, a count, a tier. Every app you put on it runs on all of them, and you pay for the machines, not the apps. {{slots}} Then slots. A slot is the same app at a second address, with settings of its own. The shop's next version waits there, on production's machines, where the developers can call it first. {{swap}} Then the swap. Staging is restarted with production's settings, warmed up, and only then does the routing change. You will run a shop that is slow to be ready, and watch it answer 503 for six seconds. A check that accepts any answer would have called it ready. {{bicep}} None of this exists without a subscription. So you will declare the plan, the app and the slot in Bicep, and read what the compiler lets through. {{fit}} And last, where App Service fits beside Container Apps and AKS.
